# Rule catalogue

<!-- Generated by tools/make_rules_doc.py from the rule specs; do not edit by hand. -->

One row per rule of the checking layer (108 rules in 51 spec files), with the calibration that
decides whether a rule may block a call. Generated by `tools/make_rules_doc.py` from the specs and
the promotion table in [`src/biowarden/engine/specs/`](../src/biowarden/engine/specs/) and from
[`family_rules.json`](../src/biowarden/bench/tasks/family_rules.json); do not edit by hand.
`python tools/make_rules_doc.py --check` fails when this page is out of date.

What a rule is, the tiers, and how verdicts become allow, warn or block:
[architecture](architecture.md). The benchmark tasks the rules are written for:
[task families](families.md).

108 rules: 79 call rules and 29 fact rules; 12 in tier T0, 96 in T1, 0 in T2. A declaration is
required by 9 rules, optional for 89 and absent for 10.

Calibration: in the default `promoted` mode 108 rules block and 0 only warn. Per rule, 600 to 19,200
correct declared calls were tested and 0 of them failed; the upper bound of the false-block rate is
at most 0.61%. **The instances are generated by the benchmark's own code, so these false-block rates
are optimistic.**

## Columns

Calibration builds benchmark workspaces from seeds, makes calls on them and labels each call by
running the real tool: a correct call has a result that is right for the workspace, a wrong call one
that is not. The engine judges the calls both with the rule's declaration and without it.

- **Rule**: the rule id, `<tool or topic>.<name>`, linked to the spec file that defines it.
- **Watches**: for a call rule, the programs it applies to, with their subcommands (their number
  when there are more than 6) and, for 27 rules, the options it needs: it applies only to a call
  that has at least one of them (their number when there are more than 8). For a fact rule, the file
  names it reads, as globs (a compressed copy, `.gz` or `.bgz`, is matched too where the pattern in
  the spec allows it), and the programs it applies to. Where a pattern ignores case
  (`featurecounts.counts_unit`), the glob is shown in lower case.
- **Programs**: `any program` means that the rule names no program. The PATH shim and `biowarden`
  ask the engine only about the programs that rules name and the interpreters `awk`, `gawk`, `mawk`,
  `perl`, `python`, `python-bio`, `python-sc`, `python-struct`, `python3`, `Rscript`; the
  whole-command pre-check asks about every simple command of the string (the first 200).
  `python-sc`, `python-struct` and `python-bio` are the Python interpreters of the single-cell,
  protein-structure and sequencing-tool environments of [supported tools](supported-tools.md).
- **Convention**: the convention slot the rule guards, with the names used in the Convention column
  of [task families](families.md).
- **Tier**: T0 decides from the call alone and reads no file; T1 may read files and run the real
  tool for a dry run; T2 can only warn.
- **Kind**: `call`: the rule applies to a call of a listed program and decides from its arguments
  and, in tier T1, from files. `fact`: the rule applies when an argument, or code inside one, names
  an existing file of a listed kind; it reads the file and fires only when the data are in a risky
  state.
- **Declaration**: `required`: a call without `--declare key=value` fails the rule. `optional`: the
  rule asks for the declaration only when the call or the data are risky. `none`: the rule has no
  declaration.
- **Families**: the families whose trap the rule is written for, from
  [`family_rules.json`](../src/biowarden/bench/tasks/family_rules.json), with the seeds or the route
  where the rule covers only part of a family. `none`: no family lists the rule as its own.
- **Mode**: what a failing rule does in the default `promoted` mode: `block`, or `warn` (the message
  is shown and the call runs). A rule blocks only when calibration admits it: it fails at least one
  wrong call, fails none of the correct calls tested (those that carry the declaration and, for a
  rule that does not require one, those without it), and the upper bound below is at most 2% over at
  least 200 such calls. A T2 rule, or a rule whose spec changed after it was measured, only warns.
- **Seeds**: the seeds of the generated instances the rule was measured on.
- **False blocks**: correct calls that carry the rule's declaration and that the rule failed, out of
  the correct declared calls tested (for a rule without a declaration, all its correct calls). A
  call tested with several values of the declaration counts once per value.
- **Upper bound**: the upper end of the exact (Clopper-Pearson) two-sided 95% confidence interval of
  the false-block rate, which treats the tested calls as independent.
- **Recall**: the wrong calls the rule failed, out of all wrong calls tested, with and without the
  declaration (a rule without a declaration counts each call once). Some of these calls are wrong
  for a reason the rule is not meant to catch, so recall is not the share of the rule's own faults
  that it catches.
